items.title: Morning Briefing: Nov. 11
items.excerpt: 11 November 2026• Update: 11 November 2026 WASHINGTON Here’s a rundown of all the news you need to start your Wednesday, including US House blocking effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, COP31 leaders’ summit set to open in Türkiye with electrification in focus, and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio calling US-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi "very productive." The US House of Representatives on Tuesday voted 211-204 to send a resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee, effectively killing the effort. Republicans backed the motion 210-1 and were joined by the chamber’s lone independent, while all 203 Democrats who voted opposed it. Republican Congressman Thomas Massie, who authored the resolution, was the only Republican to vote against it. Massie’s resolution, introduced Monday, contained eight articles of impeachment. They accuse Hegseth of waging war with Iran without congressional authorization, carrying out extrajudicial killings in airstrikes against alleged drug-trafficking vessels in the Caribbean Sea, illegally seizing then-Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, targeting Democratic Senator Mark Kelly and carrying out an unlawful war in Yemen. Hegseth dismissed the effort at a Pentagon news conference earlier Tuesday. - COP31 leaders’ summit set to open in Türkiye with electrification in focus World leaders are set to gather in Türkiye’s Mediterranean city of Antalya on Wednesday for a two-day summit at the COP31 UN climate conference, with the Turkish presidency putting electrification at the center of its push to turn climate pledges into action. Türkiye is seeking support for a proposal to raise electricity’s share of global energy use to 35% by 2035. Turkish Erdogan and UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres are scheduled to address the opening session at the Antalya Expo Center at 12.15 p.m. local time (0915GMT). National statements are due to begin at 2.30 p.m. and continue Thursday. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, whose country hosted last year’s climate talks, is among those expected to speak Wednesday, along with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Chinese Vice President Han Zheng and Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian are also expected to address the summit. - US Secretary of State Rubio describes Abu Dhabi talks between US, Russia, Ukraine as 'very productive' US Secretary of State Marco Rubio characterized trilateral negotiations between the US, Russia and Ukraine in Abu Dhabi as "very productive," saying their diplomatic efforts are looking to construct durable security arrangements. "There's a lot of work to be done in that regard. It's not like something that's on the verge of being solved in the next 24 hours or anything like that," Rubio told reporters at a G7 ministerial meeting in France. Rubio said Russian representatives agreeing to the trilateral format and showing up is "good."

items.title: Inflation runs hotter than expected as higher prices extend beyond the gas station | PBS News
items.excerpt: The consumer price index rose 0.4% from September to October, the Labor Department said Tuesday, down from 0.6% the previous month. The government did not report a yearly inflation rate because last year's government shutdown meant no data was released for October 2025. But excluding the volatile food and energy categories, core prices rose 0.3%, the same as the preceding month. Both figures were a tenth of a point higher than forecast, and at an annual rate would be well above the Fed's 2% target. The new inflation data heightened concerns that strong consumer and business spending, combined with higher gas prices and supply disruptions stemming from tariffs and global turmoil, are creating increasingly stubborn inflation that could extend beyond temporary spikes in prices at the gas pump. The economy expanded at a 3.4% annual rate in the July-September quarter, mostly driven by consumer spending. "It's worrisome. There is a sense that inflation is broad, persistent, a little bit everywhere," said Riccardo Trezzi, founder of Underlying Inflation, a consulting firm, and a former Fed economist. ... Gas prices rose 1% from September to October, the government said, a stiff increase but still much lower than in previous months. Gas prices have soared more than 37% from a year ago. ... Yet there are signs higher energy prices are spreading into other parts of the economy, with air fares, public transportation, and delivery services all jumping in price. ... Beef prices rose ... Rising shipping prices, driven up by more expensive gas, have lifted costs for restaurants and grocery stores, which may be passing them on to consumers.

items.title: Fed officials open door to a quicker round of rate hikes as inflation worsens | live
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 10 (Reuters) - The odds that the Federal Reserve may raise interest rates by half a percentage point next month jumped on Tuesday after US data showed prices rising faster than expected in October and policymakers opened the door to a quicker pace of rate hikes. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% on a monthly basis in October, down from the 0.6% registered in September as energy inflation receded. The core index excluding volatile food and energy prices, however, rose 0.3% for the third month in a row, evidence of persistent underlying inflation and price pressures spreading through the economy. A few hours before the data was released, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he planned to support a quarter-point increase at the Fed's December 8-9 meeting unless core CPI came in at 0.3% or more. "In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting," he said at a conference in London hosted by King's Business School and the Money Macro and Finance Society. Sticking with a smaller rate increase, Waller said, risked hurting the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility, given inflation was too high and appeared to be broadening. Economists polled by Reuters had expected core monthly inflation to drop to 0.2% in October. The CPI data and Waller's comments drove a powerful selloff in the US Treasury market, with the yield on 2-year notes — a proxy for Fed policy expectations — rising by the most since early April 2025. By mid-morning, market pricing reflected about a 15% chance of a half-point rate hike before retreating to about 10% in the late afternoon. Over the course of the day, traders also piled into bets the Fed would keep to its usual quarter-point rate hikes but deliver three of them by mid-2027, rather than two as seen before the data. ... Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said in separate remarks at an energy conference that it "may be possible to move more rapidly" than the pace implied by the quarter-percentage-point hike approved in September followed by a hold at the following meeting, in October. Logan said she feels the Fed needs to raise rates by at least half a percentage point more before pausing to take stock.

items.title: Up First briefing: Pete Hegseth; Jim Jordan; Iran-backed terrorists : NPR
items.excerpt: The House has effectively killed Republican Rep. Thomas Massie's effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The chamber voted 211 to 204 to send the impeachment articles back to the House Judiciary Committee for review. The move circumvents any potential floor vote on the impeachment and virtually ensures it won't be addressed before the current Congress session ends. Massie had reintroduced the impeachment articles on Monday, accusing Hegseth of high crimes related to the war with Iran and U.S. strikes against drug boats in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific. ... - 🎧 NPR's Eric McDaniel describes yesterday's vote to Up First as a game of attendance. There were enough Democrats in Washington to pass the impeachment resolution, but not enough were on the floor to vote, so Republicans had the simple majority. McDaniel spoke to Warren Davidson, a GOP congressman from Ohio, the day before the vote. Davidson said he thinks the war in Iran is unconstitutional, but argued that Hegseth was just a scapegoat for the "status quo politics in Washington." ... U.S. federal prosecutors have indicted three men accused of being Iran-backed operatives allegedly involved in nearly 20 terrorist attacks and attempted attacks in Europe and the U.S. The charges include a plot in September against a British air base where American forces were stationed. The Justice Department says some of these attacks were directed live via FaceTime from Iraq. - 🎧 Federal prosecutors in Manhattan accuse the men of working for Iran's Revolutionary Guard and the Iraqi militia Kata'ib Hezbollah, both classified as terrorist groups, according to reporter Willem Marx. Seven of the attacks happened in Britain. They included arson, explosives and a near-fatal stabbing of two Jewish men in London. Marx also noted that, in a separate case, British counter-terrorism police have arrested a 41-year-old U.S. Army soldier on suspicion of spying for Russia under the National Security Act. Authorities emphasized that this spying investigation is not linked to the Iran-related case. But Marx says these incidents raise significant concerns about security around American military bases in Britain and the safety of nearby residents.

He died on 5 November 2026, and the death was announced the following day by Abubakar Yakubu, National President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria. ## Trailers and first looks HBO’s three character posters for Harry Potter give each of the young leads the same treatment: Dominic McLaughlin as Harry, Arabella Stanton as Hermione and Alastair Stout as Ron, wands held upright down the centre of the frame under the line “The first year begins”. The motion versions carry a first snippet of Hans Zimmer’s score, and the eight-episode first season, Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone, premieres on 25 December 2026 on HBO and HBO Max. Disney and National Geographic have announced The Real Frozen, a natural history series in which Idina Menzel, Kristen Bell and Jonathan Groff return to narrate, with Josh Gad making special appearances as Olaf. It will air on National Geographic and Disney+, and no premiere date has been announced. Salman Khan shared the official trailer for Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace online on 10 November 2026. The war drama, inspired by the June 2020 Galwan Valley clash and directed by Apoorva Lakhia, opens in cinemas on 4 December 2026. The theatrical trailer for Gunmaaster G9 is due out today, 11 November 2026, ahead of the Emraan Hashmi romantic action film’s cinema release on 27 November 2026. Danny Boyle’s Ink, a drama about the birth of The Sun newspaper, has a new trailer, with Guy Pearce as Rupert Murdoch and Jack O’Connell as Larry Lamb. It opens in UK and Ireland cinemas on 8 January 2027. Jesse Eisenberg’s The Debut also has a new trailer, starring Julianne Moore and Paul Giamatti alongside Halle Bailey, ahead of its theatrical release on 11 December 2026. Dario Russo’s comedy The Fox follows the same pattern, its new trailer putting Jai Courtney and Emily Browning front and centre, with Olivia Colman and Sam Neill in one of his final performances, for a 4 December 2026 cinema release. Mouli’s dark comedy DNK, about robbery and crime, has its trailer out ahead of a 13 November 2026 cinema release. Ravi Teja launched the trailer.

items.excerpt: Jordan Firstman has been a lot of things, but 'Club Kid' confirms he's a filmmaker NEW YORK (AP) — It’s taken some time but Jordan Firstman, with “Club Kid,” feels like he’s finally made it. Since its debut at the Cannes Film Festival, “Club Kid” has been a sensation. Now, he just needs to stay on his game. The film, which Firstman wrote, directed and stars in, draws from Firstman's own experiences with gay nightlife. His character is hard-partying, hard-drug user who's shocked to discover he has a 10-year-old son. After a bidding war, A24 picked it up for $17 million and is releasing the film in the heart of awards season. Firstman has been a provocative viral-video star, a TV series writer, an actor and more. But “Club Kid” confirms he's a filmmaker. What goes in to making hit Netflix period drama 'The Empress'? Thousands of candles, wigs and extras German period drama “The Empress” has been a big hit outside of Europe. That's despite the show following the rise and reign of Empress Elisabeth of the Austrian empire. Star Devrim Lingnau Islamoğlu says she's even been recognized in Peru. And showrunner Katharina Eyssen says she's been contacted on social media from fans as far afield as Ukraine, Iran and Africa. Philip Froissant portrays Emperor Franz Joseph I and has messages from followers who have visited the real palaces where the couple lived after seeing the program. “The Empress” returns for the third and final season on Thursday. Broadway finds its Prince: Jordan Fisher cast as 'The Kid' in 'Purple Rain' musical NEW YORK (AP) — Jordan Fisher will star in the Broadway adaptation of “Purple Rain” as “The Kid.” The musical is set to premiere next spring at the Majestic Theatre, with previews starting in March. Additional casting details will be announced later. “Purple Rain” tells the story of a rising rock musician in Minneapolis who's dealing with a challenging home life and a new romance. The film's soundtrack, featuring hits like “Let’s Go Crazy” and “When Doves Cry,” won two Grammys. This role marks Fisher's first original Broadway role. Prince, who inspired the story, died in 2016. Walliams and Brand were leading UK comics. Now they are part of a reckoning over sexual misconduct LONDON (AP) — A day after British actor-comedian Russell Brand was sent to prison for rape and sexual assault, allegations have surfaced against another leading comedian, David Walliams. The cases have sparked a wider reckoning about celebrity misconduct in the U.K. Walliams, a feted children's author and well-known TV personality, is facing allegations of using his fame to exploit young female fans. He had sought to block news organizations from publishing these claims, but a judge dismissed his bid. Walliams has not been charged, but the revelations have prompted questions about the media and entertainment industries' roles in enabling such behavior. Authorities are now urging stronger protections for women.
